defaults.permitted_development: In Scotland, gates, fences, walls and other means of enclosure usually benefit from permitted development up to 2 metres high, or only 1 metre where they front a road or come forward of the principal or side elevation nearest a road.

rules.height_rules: The usual Scottish height limits are 2 metres generally and 1 metre where the enclosure fronts a road or sits forward of the principal elevation or side elevation nearest a road.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate Scottish depth allowance for fences and walls. Height and position, especially in relation to roads, do the main planning work.
rules.boundary_rules: Road-facing boundary positions are the sensitive Scottish cases. A wall that is fine in a rear garden can need permission if it comes forward of the principal elevation or fronts the road.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate Scottish roof allowance for a means of enclosure. Covered gate features or canopies should be considered separately.
rules.materials_rules: Scottish national guidance focuses on height and siting rather than prescribing materials, but prominent front boundaries are easiest to support when the finish suits the house and street.

rules.permitted_development: For a house in Scotland, the normal boundary rule is 2 metres high in general positions and 1 metre where the enclosure fronts a road or projects in front of the main road-facing elevations.

rules.height_rules: The usual Scottish height limits are 2 metres generally and 1 metre where the enclosure fronts a road or sits forward of the principal elevation or side elevation nearest a road.
rules.depth_rules: Enclosures are not assessed by projection in the same way as extensions. Once height and road relationship are known, thickness is rarely the deciding issue.
rules.boundary_rules: Road-facing boundary positions are the sensitive Scottish cases. A wall that is fine in a rear garden can need permission if it comes forward of the principal elevation or fronts the road.
rules.roof_rules: Roof form is not part of the normal enclosure right in Scotland. If the proposal adds a canopy or covered entrance element, treat that as a separate issue.
rules.materials_rules: There is no fixed Scottish material list for fences and walls, though conservation areas and listed-building settings will usually expect a more sensitive boundary treatment.

restrictions.conservation_area: In Scotland there are no normal householder permitted development rights for new fences, walls and gates in a conservation area.
restrictions.listed_building: There are no normal householder permitted development rights for boundary works within the curtilage of a listed building, and listed building consent may also be required.

rules.depth_rules: Enclosures are not assessed by projection in the same way as extensions. Once height and road relationship are known, thickness is rarely the deciding issue.
rules.boundary_rules: The boundary relationship with the road usually decides the answer. Front and corner plots in Scotland are subject to much tighter enclosure limits than enclosed garden positions.
rules.roof_rules: A wall or gate does not get a roof entitlement of its own. Scottish planning risk rises once a boundary feature becomes a covered structure.
rules.materials_rules: There is no fixed Scottish material list for fences and walls, though conservation areas and listed-building settings will usually expect a more sensitive boundary treatment.

restrictions.conservation_area: In Scotland there are no normal householder permitted development rights for new fences, walls and gates in a conservation area.
restrictions.listed_building: There are no normal householder permitted development rights for boundary works within the curtilage of a listed building, and listed building consent may also be required.

rules.permitted_development: For a house in Scotland, the normal boundary rule is 2 metres high in general positions and 1 metre where the enclosure fronts a road or projects in front of the main road-facing elevations.

rules.height_rules: The usual Scottish height limits are 2 metres generally and 1 metre where the enclosure fronts a road or sits forward of the principal elevation or side elevation nearest a road.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate Scottish depth allowance for fences and walls. Height and position, especially in relation to roads, do the main planning work.
rules.boundary_rules: Road-facing boundary positions are the sensitive Scottish cases. A wall that is fine in a rear garden can need permission if it comes forward of the principal elevation or fronts the road.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate Scottish roof allowance for a means of enclosure. Covered gate features or canopies should be considered separately.
